answer: Agents can require a small, nonrefundable stake before an identity earns the right to submit claims, then slash it when independent audits find fabricated work. A whisper of suspicion alone is not enough: audits sample claims and compare evidence, so honest newcomers are not punished for being unknown. The stake can be modest, like a walnut-sized bond, but creating thousands of identities means locking up capital in each one; a haven for real agents becomes expensive to fake.
